cues.en: One way to think about the function e to the t is to ask what properties does it have. Probably the most important one, and from some points of view, the defining property,
cues.zh: 思考 e^t 这个函数的一种方式，是问它具备哪些性质。大概最重要的一个，而且从某些角度看也是定义性的性质，

cues.en: is that it is its own derivative.
cues.zh: 就是它的导数就是它自身。

cues.en: Together with the added condition that inputting zero returns one, it's actually the only function with this property. And you can illustrate what this means with a physical model. If e to the t describes your position on a number line as a function of time, then you start at the number one. And what this equation is saying is that your velocity,
cues.zh: 再加上输入 0 时返回 1 这个附加条件，它实际上是唯一具有这一性质的函数。你可以用一个物理模型来说明这意味着什么。如果 e^t 描述你在数轴上随时间变化的位置，那么你从数字 1 开始。而这个方程说的是，你的速度，

cues.en: the derivative of position, is always equal to that position.
cues.zh: 也就是位置的导数，始终等于那个位置。

cues.en: The farther away from zero you are, the faster you move. So even before knowing how to compute e to the t exactly,
cues.zh: 你离零越远，移动得就越快。所以，即使还不知道如何精确计算 e^t，

cues.en: going from a specific time to a specific position, this ability to associate each position with a velocity paints a very strong intuitive picture of how the function must grow. You know that you'll be accelerating and at an accelerating rate with an all around feeling of things getting out of hand quickly.
cues.zh: 从特定时间到特定位置，这种把每个位置与速度对应起来的能力，非常直观地描绘出这个函数必然如何增长。你会知道自己正在加速，而且加速度还在变大，整体感觉就是事情很快就会失控。

cues.en: And if you add a constant to that exponent, like e to the two times t, the chain rule tells us that the derivative is now two times itself.
cues.zh: 如果你在这个指数上加一个常数，比如 e 的 2t 次方，链式法则告诉我们，它的导数现在是自身的两倍。

cues.en: So at every point on the number line, rather than attaching a vector corresponding to the number itself, first, double the magnitude of the position,
cues.zh: 所以在数轴上的每个点，不是直接附上一个对应这个数本身的向量，而是先把位置的幅值加倍，

cues.en: then attach it. Moving so that your position is always e to the two t is the same thing as moving in such a way that your velocity
cues.zh: 再把它附上去。让你的位置始终是 e 的 2t 次方的移动，等价于以这样的方式移动：你的速度

cues.en: is always twice your position.
cues.zh: 始终是你位置的两倍。

cues.en: The implication of that too is that our runaway growth feels all the more out of control.
cues.zh: 这也意味着，我们这种失控式增长会让人更觉得无法掌控。

cues.en: If that constant was negative, say negative 0.5,
cues.zh: 如果那个常数是负的，比如 -0.5，

cues.en: then your velocity vector is always negative 0.5 times your position vector, meaning you flip it around a 180 degrees and scale its length by a half.
cues.zh: 那么你的速度向量就始终是位置向量的 -0.5 倍，也就是说把方向翻转 180 度，再把长度缩小一半。

cues.en: Moving in such a way that your velocity always matches this flipped and squished copy of your position vector, you'd go the other direction,
cues.zh: 如果以这种方式运动，让速度始终等于位置向量翻转并压缩后的副本，你就会朝相反方向走，

cues.en: slowing down in an exponential decay towards zero.
cues.zh: 以指数衰减的方式减速，趋近于零。

cues.en: But what about if that constant was I, the square root of negative one?
cues.zh: 但如果那个常数是 I，也就是负一的平方根呢？

cues.en: If your position was always e to the I t, how would you move as the time t ticks forward?
cues.zh: 如果你的位置始终是 e 的 I t 次方，那么随着时间 t 向前推进，你会怎样移动？

cues.en: Well, now the derivative of your position will always be I times itself, and multiplying by I has the effect of rotating numbers 90 degrees.
cues.zh: 这时你位置的导数就始终是 I 乘以它自身，而乘以 I 的效果是把数旋转 90 度。

cues.en: So as you might expect, things only make sense here if we start thinking beyond the number line and in the complex plane.
cues.zh: 所以如你所料，只有当我们跳出数轴、开始在复平面里思考，这一切才说得通。

cues.en: So even before you know how to compute e to the I times t, you know that for any position this might give for some value of time, the velocity at that time will be a 90 degree rotation of that position.
cues.zh: 所以，即使你还不知道怎么计算 e 的 i·t 次方，你也知道：对它在某个时刻可能给出的任意位置，那个时刻的速度就是该位置旋转 90 度。

cues.en: Drawing this for all possible positions you might come across, you get a vector field where as usual with vector fields, you shrink things down to avoid clutter.
cues.zh: 把所有你可能遇到的位置都画出来，就得到一个向量场；和通常的向量场一样，为了不显得杂乱，我们会把箭头缩小。

cues.en: At time t equals zero, e to the I t will be one. That's our initial condition. And there's only one trajectory starting from that position where your velocity is always matching the vector that it's passing through, a 90 degree rotation of the position.
cues.zh: 当 t 等于 0 时，e 的 i·t 次方等于 1，这就是我们的初始条件。而从那个位置出发，只有一条轨迹能让速度始终与它所经过的向量保持一致，也就是位置旋转 90 度。

cues.en: It's when you go around a circle of radius one at a speed of one unit per second.
cues.zh: 就是当你以每秒一个单位的速度绕半径为 1 的圆运动时。

cues.en: So after pi seconds, you've traced a distance of pi around,
cues.zh: 所以经过 π 秒后，你沿圆周走过了 π 的距离，

cues.en: so e to the I times pi should be negative one.
cues.zh: 所以 e 的 iπ 次方应该等于 -1。

cues.en: After tau seconds, you've gone full circle.
cues.zh: 经过 τ 秒后，你转了一整圈。

cues.en: E to the I times tau equals one.
cues.zh: e 的 iτ 次方等于 1。

cues.en: And more generally, e to the I times t equals a number that's t radians around this unit circle in the complex plane.
cues.zh: 更一般地，e 的 it 次方等于复平面上沿这个单位圆转过 t 弧度的那个数。

cues.en: Nevertheless, something might still feel immoral about putting an imaginary number up in that exponent, and you would be right to question that. What we write as e to the t is a bit of a notational disaster,
cues.zh: 不过，把虚数放到那个指数上，可能仍让人觉得有点不道德，而你有理由质疑这一点。我们写成 e 的 t 次方，在记号上有点灾难，

cues.en: giving the number e and the idea of repeated multiplication
cues.zh: 让数字 e 和重复相乘的想法

cues.en: way more emphasis than they deserve.
cues.zh: 得到了远超它们应得的强调。

cues.en: But my time is up, so I'll spare you the full rant until the next video.
cues.zh: 不过我的时间到了，就不让你们听我长篇大论了，留到下个视频吧。
